acceptedInterpretation: The request 'change our command tool name from lattice to proof-or-stop, replacing all lattice wording in the documentation' is read as: rename every FORWARD-LOOKING surface, and leave historical records and signature-bearing identifiers frozen. Concretely IN: the user-facing bin name (proof-or-stop becomes primary, lattice retained as a working deprecated alias), active documentation prose and command examples (~183 files), and the CLI's own forward-looking output strings (help/usage text, session-brief header, error hints). Concretely OUT: the 391 story archives under .lattice/story/ and CHANGELOG.md (both record what already happened), the 13 signature salt literals (hashed into _hash fields on live artifacts, so renaming invalidates every stored signature), the .lattice/ state directory, the 13 lattice-prefixed agent role IDs (subagent_type values; a separate consolidation plan owns their migration), the npm package names (renaming @lattice/core silently self-disarms the pre-push recursive-tsc gate), lattice.config.json, the LATTICE_* env prefix, the managed-block markers and the push-approval schema literal. The word 'all' in the original request was the main ambiguity: read literally it would include salts and archives, which would invalidate all stored signatures and falsify the audit trail. The user resolved this ambiguity explicitly when asked, saying the rename 'should influence current state or future works, not past works or history, so I think it's the former', which is the authority for the boundary above. The competing interpretation - full literal identifier rename - is therefore recorded as rejected-by-user rather than merely unimplemented, and remains available as a future story with its own signature-migration design.
notes: High-assurance collision resolved against an explicit user ruling rather than an assistant assumption. Independent corroboration that the chosen breadth is correct rather than convenient: README.md:96 already declared 'lattice is the CLI command name for historical reasons; the project is Proof-or-Stop ... a rename in progress', so the in-scope half completes a rename the repo had already committed to. Two decision docs were checked for conflict and resolved as OQ-1 and OQ-2 via scope_question_resolve: proof-or-stop-agent-prompt-consolidation-execution-plan.md:36-43 owns the role-ID half (complementary scope, not contradiction), and lifecycle-artifact-scope.md:217 was found to be a stale pre-rename snapshot (zero proof-or-stop mentions in that file) that CHK-003 now updates.
